items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: Jim Crow playing the trombone. That's right. The night we made it recorded.

ctx.x: And the Navy Dodds was supposed to be there. Be there, yeah. He had his arm or something so they got me there. Yeah, he got me that last minute to come and record. Still had on your uniform, I remember.

Yeah, yeah, it was a night at the old artesian hall, called the Night in New Orleans. I made a recording that night. It was Wooden Joe, they weren't there playing... Yes, Wooden Joe and Burbank and Lawrence. Lawrence and we had Boots playing trombones, playing the bass. Jim Crow playing the trombone. That's right. The night we made it recorded.
And you got out of the Navy then just a few months after that in August.

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: The remainder of George Lewis' band, who was remaining was Kid Howard, Jim. So we got Emma to play piano

ctx.x: It was Lawrence Murray's band, was it?

Yeah, it was Lawrence Murray. He couldn't go on to George Lewis' title because it was an organized band. But George, George Rosenthal told him, let's get him a good city. But he know most of the men's coming up there because he was down here. He came down here when we even was working at the paddock. Then we made another group. We come out the paddock, we made another group. When George, one time George Lewis split his band. Some of these men that won't go on the road like, such as Jim Crow and Kid Howard, with…
Well, uh, Bro. Well, uh, Bro.
